cards.front: Define hardware.
back: The physical components of a computer system.

cards.front: Which logic gate outputs 1 only when its two inputs are different?
back: XOR.

cards.front: Which CPU component performs calculations and logical comparisons?
back: Arithmetic logic unit (ALU).

cards.front: Which translator converts assembly language into machine code?
back: Assembler.

cards.front: Name the volatile main memory used for active programs and data.
back: RAM.

cards.front: What is an embedded system?
back: A computer built into a larger device to perform a dedicated or limited function.

cards.front: Explain the relationship between hardware and software.
back: Software supplies instructions and data that control operations.
Hardware provides the physical components that execute those instructions.

cards.front: Explain the difference between system software and application software.
back: System software manages computer resources and provides a platform.
Application software performs tasks for the end user.

cards.front: Give two functions of an operating system.
back: Any two of processor scheduling, memory management, device/I/O management, application management, file management or security.

cards.front: Explain the difference between machine code and assembly language.
back: Machine code is binary executed directly by a particular processor.
Assembly uses mnemonic instructions with a one-to-one correspondence to machine-code instructions.

cards.front: Explain the difference between volatile and non-volatile memory.
back: Volatile memory loses its contents when power is removed.
Non-volatile memory retains its contents without power.

cards.front: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of cloud storage compared with local storage.
back: It can be accessed from different locations and can provide off-site backup.
It depends on connectivity/provider availability or may create privacy and ongoing-cost concerns.

cards.front: Give the outputs of AND, OR and XOR when A = 1 and B = 1.
back: AND = 1.
OR = 1.
XOR = 0.

cards.front: Describe the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
back: Fetch the next instruction from main memory into the CPU.
Decode it to determine the required operation.
Execute the instruction, including any required read or write.

cards.front: Explain how cache size can affect CPU performance.
back: Cache stores frequently used instructions and data close to the CPU.
A larger cache can hold more of this data.
This can reduce slower accesses to main memory and improve performance.

cards.front: Compare RAM and ROM.
back: RAM is volatile and stores programs/data currently in use.
ROM is non-volatile and stores instructions or data that must persist.
Both provide electronic storage used by the computer system.

cards.front: Give three advantages of high-level languages over low-level languages.
back: They are easier for people to read and write.
Programs are faster to develop, test and maintain.
The source can usually be translated for different processor types.

cards.front: Explain why an SSD is suitable for a laptop.
back: It has no moving parts, so it is resistant to physical shock.
It provides fast access to programs and data.
It is quiet and generally uses less power than magnetic storage.

cards.front: Compare a compiler and an interpreter.
back: A compiler translates the whole high-level program and produces machine/object code.
The translated program can run later without translating every statement again.
An interpreter processes statements while the program runs and does not directly create a machine-code program.
Interpretation supports quick testing but requires the interpreter and may be slower during repeated execution.

cards.front: Explain the roles of the ALU, control unit, clock and registers.
back: The ALU performs arithmetic and logical operations.
The control unit coordinates instruction processing and sends control signals.
The clock supplies timing signals that synchronise operations.
Registers hold immediate instructions, data or intermediate results inside the CPU.

cards.front: Compare magnetic and solid-state secondary storage.
back: Magnetic storage magnetises a surface and often contains moving parts.
It normally gives high capacity at a lower cost per gigabyte.
Solid-state storage uses electronic circuits with no moving parts, so it is faster and more resistant to shock.
Solid state often costs more per gigabyte and has limited write endurance.

cards.front: Explain how clock speed, cores and cache can affect CPU performance.
back: Higher clock speed allows more cycles each second.
Multiple cores can process more tasks simultaneously when software supports parallel work.
Larger cache reduces time spent waiting for main memory.
Overall improvement depends on the workload, software and other system bottlenecks.
